metadata.name: Tactile Pushbutton (6mm)
metadata.description: A momentary tactile pushbutton switch - normally open, closes when pressed
metadata.author: tigoe

connectionGuide.purpose: One terminal of the momentary push button. When pressed, this connects electrically to the other terminal (leg1). Typically connects to the GPIO input pin.
warnings: Buttons are NOT polarized - either leg can connect to either side
ALWAYS use a pull-down resistor (10kΩ to GND) for stable readings
Without pull-down, the GPIO will 'float' and give random readings
troubleshooting: If readings are random: check that 10kΩ pull-down resistor connects this bus to GND
If button seems always pressed: check for shorts or wrong wiring
If button seems always released: verify 3.3V connects to the OTHER leg
Add software debouncing (10-50ms delay) to avoid multiple triggers per press

connectionGuide.purpose: Other terminal of the push button. In a typical pull-DOWN configuration, this leg connects to 3.3V power. When pressed, 3.3V flows through to the GPIO pin.
warnings: Connect to 3.3V (not 5V) when using with Raspberry Pi Pico
Do NOT connect button directly between 3.3V and GND (short circuit!)
troubleshooting: Typical wiring: leg0 → GPIO + 10kΩ to GND, leg1 → 3.3V
Pressed = HIGH (1), Released = LOW (0) with pull-down config
If behavior is inverted, you may have pull-UP instead of pull-DOWN

recommendedPullResistor.description: 10kΩ from button to ground for stable LOW state

warnings: Button requires pull-down or pull-up resistor for stable readings
Typical configuration: GPIO → Button → 3.3V, with 10kΩ pull-down to GND
Alternative: Use Pico internal pull-down (software configuration)
Do not connect button directly between power and ground
